Subject: Children's ibuprofen recall: what parents need to know

Important for parents: Corvane children's ibuprofen recall

A lot of you have been asking about this since last night, so here is what happened and what to do.

The issue is the dosing syringe in the box, not the medicine. Corvane has recalled the syringe that came with Pediatric Ibuprofen Oral Suspension 100 mg/5 mL (berry flavour, 120 mL bottle). The numbers printed on the syringe are wrong, so every mark measures double what it says. The line marked 2.5 mL actually holds 5 mL. The line marked 5 mL actually holds 10 mL. If you used that syringe and followed the markings, your child got about twice the intended dose.

The liquid itself is fine. The manufacturer has confirmed it meets all specifications and is not contaminated. Expiry is 08/2027.

Check your box first
Look at the lot number on the bottom of the box. The affected lots are:
CV6114A
CV6114B
If your box is Corvane and has either of these lot numbers, throw out the syringe that came with it. Don't use it again, even if you plan to "just use half."

Free replacement syringes
New, correctly marked 10 mL oral syringes arrive today (Monday) before noon. They are free for anyone who needs one. You don't need a receipt and you don't need to have bought the medicine here. Just come in and ask. If you'd rather return the product, Corvane is offering a full refund.

We'll also be open this Saturday, Nov 14, from 10 to 4 for exchanges and questions.

If you think your child got a double dose
Call the poison centre at 1-844-POISON-X (1-844-764-7669). It's free and open 24/7. They'll ask about your child's weight, how much they got, how many doses and when, and then tell you what to do. Please call them even if your child seems okay. We can't safely assess every child from a Facebook comment, because the answer depends on weight, the number of doses, and other health factors like kidney problems. The poison centre is set up to do exactly that.

Don't give another dose until the poison centre or your doctor says it's okay.

Call 911 or go to emerg right away if your child:
is very sleepy or hard to wake up
is vomiting blood
is not peeing
has a seizure

If your kids have a fever right now and haven't had the recalled syringe dose recently, you can still use the medicine with a correctly marked oral syringe. Follow the dose on the box for your child's weight or age. If you're not sure, ask us or call the poison centre.

How we handled the notice
We got the recall notice on the evening of Nov 6. On the morning of Nov 7 we pulled the affected lots off our shelf and put up signs on the front door and in the kids' aisle. Over-the-counter medicine doesn't come with a patient profile, so for most of these purchases we have no name or phone number to call. That's why we're asking everyone to check their medicine cabinet and share this post.

Our phone lines are very busy this morning. We're working through every message and we will call you back. If it's urgent and about your child's health, call the poison centre or 911. Don't wait for us.

Rania Haddad, Pharmacist
Cedarbrook Pharmacy, Erin Mills Pkwy
